<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>

<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

3dee797156:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>N</c>octe surgéntes vigilémus omnes,
Semper in psalmis meditémur, atque
Víribus totis Dómino canámus
Dúlciter hymnos.

<h>U</h>t pio Regi páriter canéntes,
Cum suis Sanctis mereámur aulam
Íngredi cæli, simul et beátam
Dúcere vitam.

<h>P</h>ræstet hoc nobis Déitas beáta
Patris, ac Nati, paritérque Sancti
Spíritus, cujus réboat per omnem
Glória mundum.
Amen.
7798d5e712:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>N</c>ow, from the slumbers of the night arising,
Chant we the holy psalmody of David,
Hymns to our Master, with a voice concordant,
Sweetly intoning.

<h>S</h>o may our Monarch pitifully hear us,
That we may merit with his saints to enter
Mansions eternal, therewithal possessing
Joy beatific.

<h>T</h>his be our portion, God forever blessed,
Father eternal, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Whose is the glory, which through all creation
Ever resoundeth.
Amen.

<c>J</c>uvenília autem desidéria sectáre vero justítiam, em, spem, caritátem, et .ni com iis, qui ínvocant Dóminum de corde puro. <h>Lesson 5</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the mercy of Christ bring us to the joys of paradise.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Ad Timotheum 2 2:22-26</r>
But flee thou youthful desires, and pursue justice, faith, charity, and peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. And avoid foolish and unlearned questions, knowing that they beget strifes. But the servant of the Lord must not wrangle: but be mild towards all men, apt to teach, patient, With modesty admonishing them that resist the truth: if peradventure God may give them repentance to know the truth, And they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Te Deum</h>
<r>Canticum SS. Ambrosii et Augustini</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * majestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ majestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Judex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
6dd1763062:
<h>Te Deum</h>
<c>W</c>e praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.
All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.
To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.
To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.
<n>bow head</n> Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;
Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.
The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.
The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.
The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.
The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;
The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.
Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;
Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.
Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.
Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.
<n>During the following verse all make a profound bow:</n> When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.
When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.
Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.
We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.
<n>Kneel for the following verse</n> We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.
Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.
O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.
Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.
Day by day * we magnify thee;
<n>During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow.</n> And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.
Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.
O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.
O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.
O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

<r>2 Thess 3</r>
<c>D</c>óminus dírigat corda et córpora nostra in caritáte Dei, et patiéntia Christi.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>L</c>ucis Creátor óptime,
Lucem diérum próferens,
Primórdiis lucis novæ,
Mundi parans oríginem:

<h>Q</h>ui mane iunctum vésperi
Diem vocári prǽcipis:
Tetrum chaos illábitur,
Audi preces cum flétibus.

<h>N</h>e mens graváta crímine,
Vitæ sit exsul múnere,
Dum nil perénne cógitat,
Seséque culpis ílligat.

<h>C</h>ælórum pulset íntimum,
Vitále tollat prǽmium:
Vitémus omne nóxium:
Purgémus omne péssimum.

<h>P</h>ræsta, Pater piíssime,
Patríque compar Únice,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito
Regnans per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

9e36b8df3d:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>2 Thess 3</r>
<c>A</c>nd the Lord direct your hearts, in the charity of God, and the patience of Christ.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> blest Creator of the light,
Who mak’st the day with radiance bright,
And o’er the forming world didst call
The light from chaos first of all;

<h>W</h>hose wisdom joined in meet array
The morn and eve, and named them day:
Night comes with all its darkling fears;
Regard thy people’s prayers and tears.

<h>L</h>est, sunk in sin, and whelmed with strife,
They lose the gift of endless life;
While thinking but the thoughts of time,
They weave new chains of woe and crime.

<h>B</h>ut grant them grace that they may strain
The heavenly gate and prize to gain:
Each harmful lure aside to cast,
And purge away each error past.

<h>O</h> Father, that we ask be done,
Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, direct my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> As incense in thy sight.

aff2c80ed5:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>T</c>e lucis ante términum,
Rerum Creátor, póscimus,
Ut sólita cleméntia
Sis præsul ad custódiam.

<h>P</h>rocul recédant sómnia,
Et nóctium phantásmata;
Hostémque nostrum cómprime,
Ne polluántur córpora.

<h>P</h>ræsta, Pater omnípotens,
Per Jesum Christum Dóminum,
Qui tecum in perpétuum
Regnat cum Sancto Spíritu.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.
08fbe66a8b:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>B</c>efore the ending of the day,
Creator of the world, we pray
That with thy wonted favor thou
Wouldst be our guard and keeper now.

<h>F</h>rom all ill dreams defend our eyes,
From nightly fears and fantasies;
Tread under foot our ghostly foe,
That no pollution we may know.

<h>O</h> Father, that we ask be done,
Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Keep us, O Lord, as the apple of thine eye.
<r>℟.</r> Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

407c332e98:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>V</c>ísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: et Ángeli tui sancti habitántes in ea nos in pace custódiant, et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
Per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti Deus: per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
f5b5bd304d:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>V</c>isit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
18164f80d9:

<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
<r>Benedictio.</r> <n>Given by the Prior, without chant (not on Maundy Thursday and Good Friday):</n> Benedíctio Dei omnipoténtis Patris, et Fílii, ✠ et Spíritus Sancti descéndat super vos, et máneat semper.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>In the absence of the Prior, the Subprior or the Hebdomadarian gives it, saying not super vos but super nos.</n>
ae06173a7e:
<h>Conclusion</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<r>℣.</r> Let us bless the Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
<r>Benediction.</r> May the blessing of almighty God, the Father, the Son, ✠ and the Holy Ghost, come down upon you and remain for ever.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
d0d30257cc:
<h>Ad processionem in fine Completorii</h>
<n>After the blessing the Salve Regina is begun by two cantors (on Doubles and Totum Duplex) or by one; at its beginning all prostrate, or kneel in Paschaltide, until "Salve Regina" has been sung; then the procession goes into the church and the Hebdomadarian sprinkles the brethren with holy water.</n>
<r>Ant.</r> Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ: Vita, dulcédo et spes nostra, salve. Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ. Ad te suspirámus, geméntes et flentes in hac lacrimárum valle. Eia ergo, advocáta nostra, illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte. Et Jesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui, nobis post hoc exsílium osténde. O clemens, O pia, O dulcis Virgo María.
<r>℣.</r> Dignáre me laudáre te, Virgo sacráta.
<r>℟.</r> Da mihi virtútem contra hostes tuos.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>C</c>oncéde nos fámulos tuos, quǽsumus, Dómine Deus, perpétua mentis et córporis salúte gaudére: et gloriósa beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis intercessióne a præsénti liberári tristítia, et ætérna pérfrui lætítia: Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> O lumen Ecclésiæ, Doctor veritátis, Rosa patiéntiæ, Ebur castitátis, Aquam sapiéntiæ propinásti gratis: Prædicátor grátiæ, nos junge beátis.
<r>℣.</r> Ora pro nobis, beáte Pater Domínice.
<r>℟.</r> Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>C</c>oncéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui peccatórum nostrórum póndere prémimur, beáti Domínici Confessóris tui, Patris nostri, patrocínio sublevémur: Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<n>Then Pater noster and Credo in Deum, said silently.</n>
66f77f2a16:
<h>Procession at the end of Compline</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve; to thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.
<r>℣.</r> Make me worthy to praise thee, holy Virgin.
<r>℟.</r> Give me strength against thine enemies.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, O Lord God, that we thy servants may enjoy perpetual health of mind and body; and by the glorious intercession of blessed Mary ever Virgin, be delivered from present sorrow and enjoy eternal gladness. Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> O light of the Church, teacher of truth, rose of patience, ivory of chastity, freely thou didst pour forth the waters of wisdom: preacher of grace, unite us with the blessed.
<r>℣.</r> Pray for us, blessed Father Dominic.
<r>℟.</r> That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that we who are weighed down by the burden of our sins may be raised up by the patronage of blessed Dominic, thy Confessor, our Father. Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>L</h>inguam refrénans témperet,

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>N</c>ow in the sun's new dawning ray,
Lowly of heart, our God we pray
That he from harm may keep us free
In all the deeds this day shall see.

<h>M</h>ay fear of him our tongues restrain,
Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:
His favouring care our guardian be,
Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

<h>M</h>ay every heart be pure from sin
And folly find no place therein:
Scant need of food, excess denied,
Wear down in us the body's pride.

<h>T</h>hat when the light of day is gone,
And night in course shall follow on.
We, free from cares the world affords,
May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

<h>A</h>ll laud to God the Father be,
All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To God the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

7ed9477f13:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Adorémus Dóminum, * Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Adorémus Dóminum, * Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Adorémus Dóminum, * Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Quóniam ipse fecit nos.
<r>Ant.</r> Adorémus Dóminum, * Quóniam ipse fecit nos.

90a297858f:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, qui fecit nos, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, qui fecit nos, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, qui fecit nos, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, qui fecit nos, * Veníte, adorémus.

d43afe2c5e:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum Deum nostrum * Veníte, adorémus.

040af19508:
<h>Lesson 7</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the Gospel reading be our salvation and protection.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew At that time, when Jesus was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him: And behold a leper came and adored him. And so on. Homily by St. Jerome, Priest (at Bethlehem.) When the Lord was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed Him. They were not able to follow Him when He went up. And first there came a leper. This poor creature's disease had prevented him from hearing the Saviour's long sermon on the Mount. Let it be noted that he is the first person specially named as being healed. The second was the Centurion's servant; the third was Peter's wife's mother, who was sick of a fever at Capernaum; the fourth were they who were brought unto Christ as being troubled with evil spirits, from whom He by His word cast out the evil spirits, at the same time that He healed all that were sick.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

Dómine, si vis, potes me mundáre. Qui voluntátem rogat, de virtúte non dúbitat. Et exténdens Jesus manum tétigit eum, dicens: Volo, mundáre. Extendénte manum Dómino, statim lepra fugit. Simúlque consídera, quam húmilis, et sine jactántia respónsio. Dominica Ii. Post Lectio ix, Lue díxerat, Si vis: Dóminus respóndit, Volo. Ille præmíserat, Potes me mundáre: Dóminus jungit, et dicit, Mundáre. Non ergo, ut pleríque Latinórum putant, jungéndum est, et legéndum, Volo mundáre: sed separátim, ut primum dicat, Volo; deínde ímperet, Mundáre. Et ait illi Jesus: Vide, némini díxeris. Et revéra quid erat necésse ut sermóne jactáret, quod córpore præferébat? Sed vade, osténde te sacerdóti. Várias ob causas mittit eum ad sacerdótem: primum propter humilitátem, ut sacerdótibus deférre honórem videátur. Erat enim lege præcéptum, ut, qui mundáti fúerant a lepra, offérrent múnera sacerdótibus. Deínde, ut mundátum vidéntes leprósum, aut créderent Salvatóri, aut non créderent: st créderent, salvaréntur; si non créderent, inexcusábiles forent. Et simul, ne, quod in eo sæpíssime criminabántur, legem viderétur infríngere.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>E</c>cce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, et suscitábo David germen justum: et regnábit rex, et sápiens erit: et fáciet judícium et justítiam in terra.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Missus est Gábriel Ángelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Joseph, núntians ei verbum: et expavéscit Virgo de lúmine. Ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Dóminum: ecce concípies, et páries, * Et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.
<r>℣.</r> Dabit ei Dóminus Deus sedem David patris ejus, et regnábit in domo Jacob in ætérnum. Et.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Et.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>C</c>ónditor alme síderum,
Ætérna lux credéntium,
Christe, Redémptor ómnium,
Exáudi preces súpplicum.

<h>Q</h>ui cóndolens intéritu
Mortis períre sǽculum,
Salvásti mundum lánguidum,
Donans reis remédium,

<h>V</h>ergénte mundi véspere,
Uti sponsus de thálamo,
Egréssus honestíssima
Vírginis matris cláusula.

<h>C</h>uius forti poténtiæ
Genu curvántur ómnia;
Cæléstia, terréstria
Nutu faténtur súbdita.

<h>T</h>e deprecámur, hágie,
Ventúre judex sǽculi,
Consérva nos in témpore
Hostis a telo pérfidi.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória,
Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Roráte, cæli, désuper, et nubes pluant justum.
<r>℟.</r> Aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.

<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Jer 23</r>
<c>B</c>ehold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign, and shall be wise, and shall execute judgement and justice in the earth.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Missus est Gábriel Ángelus ad Maríam Vírginem desponsátam Joseph, núntians ei verbum: et expavéscit Virgo de lúmine. Ne tímeas, María, invenísti grátiam apud Dóminum: ecce concípies, et páries, * Et vocábitur Altíssimi Fílius.
<r>℣.</r> The Lord God shall give unto Him the throne of His father David, and He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>B</c>right builder of the heavenly poles,
Eternal light of faithful souls,
Jesus, Redeemer of mankind,
Our humble prayers vouchsafe to mind.

<h>W</h>ho, lest the fraud of hell’s black king
Should all men to destruction bring,
Didst, by an act of generous love,
The fainting world’s physician prove.

<h>W</h>ho, that thou mightst our ransom pay
And wash the stains of sin away,
Wouldst from a Virgin’s womb proceed
And on the cross a victim bleed.

<h>W</h>hose glorious power, whose saving name
No sooner any voice can frame,
But heaven and earth and hell agree
To honour them with trembling knee.

<h>T</h>hee, Christ, who at the latter day
Shalt be our Judge, we humbly pray
Such arms of heavenly grace to send
As may thy Church from foes defend.

<h>B</h>e glory given and honour done
To God the Father and the Son
And to the Holy Ghost on high,
From age to age eternally.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the Just.
<r>℟.</r> Let the earth be opened, and bud forth the Saviour.

<c>V</c>erbum supérnum, pródiens
A Patre olim éxiens,
Qui natus orbi súbvenis,
Cursu declívi témporis.

<h>I</h>llúmina nunc péctora,
Tuóque amóre cóncrema;
Audíto ut præcónio
Sint pulsa tandem lúbrica.

<h>I</h>udéxque cum post áderis
Rimári facta péctoris,

Iustísque regnum pro bonis.

<h>N</h>on demum arctémur malis
Pro qualitáte críminis;

Simus perénnes cælibes.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória,

316493f49a:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>C</c>elestial Word, to this our earth
Sent down from God's eternal clime,
To save mankind by mortal birth
Into a world of change and time;

<h>E</h>nlighten our hearts; vain hopes destroy;
And in thy love's consuming fire
Fill all the soul with heavenly joy,
And melt the dross of low desire.

<h>S</h>o when the Judge of quick and dead
Shall bid his awful summons come,
To whelm the guilty soul with dread,
And call the blessed to their home.

<h>S</h>aved from the whirling, black abyss,
Forevermore to us be given
To share the feast of saintly bliss,
And see the face of God in heaven.

<h>T</h>o God the Father and the Son
Our songs with one accord we raise;
And to the Holy Spirit, One
With them, be ever equal praise
Amen.

<r>Jer 23</r>

<c>V</c>ox clara ecce íntonat,
Obscúra quæque íncrepat:

Ab æthre Christus prómicat.

<h>M</h>ens jam resúrgat tórpida
Quæ sorde exstat sáucia;
Sidus refúlget jam novum,
Ut tollat omne nóxium.

Laxáre gratis débitum:
Omnes pro indulgéntia
Vocem demus cum lácrimis,

Mundúmque horror cínxerit,

Sed nos pius tunc prótegat.

Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,

<c>H</c>ark, a herald voice is calling;

Let the earth-bound soul arise;
Christ, her sun, all sloth dispelling,

Wrapping all the earth in fear,
May he then as our defender
On the clouds of heaven appear.

To the Father and the Son,

Eternal light of faithful souls,

Our humble prayers vouchsafe to mind.

Should all men to destruction bring,
Didst, by an act of generous love,
The fainting world’s physician prove.

And wash the stains of sin away,

Such arms of heavenly grace to send
As may thy Church from foes defend.

And to the Holy Ghost on high,
From age to age eternally.

<n>Quo dicto, séquitur:</n>
<r>℣.</r> Jubilémus Deo salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos: quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus: <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos: quia ipse est Dóminus Deus noster: nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.

<r>℣.</r> Hódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt, et vidérunt ópera mea.

<r>℣.</r> Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde: ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.

<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 2:1-3</r>
<c>V</c>erbum, quod vidit Isaías, fílius Amos, super Juda et Jerúsalem. Et erit in novíssimis diébus præparátus mons domus Dómini in vértice móntium, et elevábitur super colles, et fluent ad eum omnes gentes. Et ibunt pópuli multi, et dicent: Veníte, et ascendámus ad montem Dómini, et ad domum Dei Jacob, et docébit nos vias suas, et ambulábimus in sémitis ejus: quia de Sion exíbit lex, et verbum Dómini de Jerúsalem.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium i</h>
<r>℟.</r> Aspíciens a longe, ecce vídeo Dei poténtiam veniéntem, et nébulam totam terram tegéntem. * Ite óbviam ei, et dícite: Núntia nobis, si tu es ipse, Qui regnatúrus es in pópulo Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Excíta, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni, ut salvos fácias nos. Ite óbviam ei.

And in the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall flow unto it. <r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium i</h>
<r>℟.</r> Ave, María, grátia plena; Dóminus tecum * Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet in te, et virtus Altíssimi obumbrábit tibi: quod enim ex te nascétur Sanctum, vocábitur Fílius Dei.
<r>℣.</r> Quómodo fiet istud, quóniam virum non cognósco? Et respóndens Angelus, dixit ei. Spíritus Sanctus supervéniet.

<r>Isa 3:1-3</r>
For behold the sovereign the Lord of hosts shall take away from Jerusalem, and from Juda the valiant and the strong, the whole strength of bread, and the whole strength of water. The strong man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the cunning man, and the ancient. The captain over fifty, and the honourable in countenance, and the counsellor, and the architect, and the skillful in eloquent speech.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. * The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee; therefore, also that Holy Thing Which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
<r>℣.</r> How shall this be, seeing I know not a man? And the Angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost.

Quod ergo Dóminus fatétur de spíritu, hoc Joánnes dénegat de persóna.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

74db8db461:
<h>Lesson 9</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the King of Angels bring us to the fellowship of the citizens of heaven.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
Let us then more minutely examine these words, and we shall find that there is no real contradiction. When the Angel announced to Zacharias the coming birth of John he said He shall go before Him in the spirit and power of Elias, (Luke i. 17.) As the old Elias will come again before the Second Advent of the Lord, so did John, as the new Elias, go before the First Advent, in the spirit and power of Elias. As the old Elias will be the Fore-runner of the Judge, so the new Elias was the Forerunner of the Saviour. John then was Elias in spirit, but not in person; and our Lord asserteth of the spirit what John denieth of the person.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

912099bc59:
<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 33:2-5</r>
<c>D</c>ómine miserére nostri: te enim exspectávimus: esto bráchium nostrum in mane, et salus nostra in témpore tribulatiónis. A voce ángeli fugérunt pópuli, et ab exaltatióne tua dispérsæ sunt gentes. Et congregabúntur spólia vestra sicut collígitur bruchus, velut cum fossæ plenæ fúerint de eo. Magnificátus est Dóminus, quóniam habitávit in excélso: implévit Sion judício et justítia.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium i</h>
<r>℟.</r> Ecce apparébit Dóminus super nubem cándidam, Et cum eo Sanctórum míllia: habens in vestiménto, et in fémore suo scriptum * Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium.
<r>℣.</r> Apparébit in finem, et non mentiétur; si moram fécerit, exspécta eum, quia véniens véniet. Rex regum, et.
61e2b294e5:
<h>Lesson 1</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the everlasting Father bless us with an everlasting blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 33:2-5</r>
O Lord, have mercy on us: for we have waited for thee: be thou our arm in the morning, and our salvation in the time of trouble. At the voice of the angel the people fled, and at the lifting up thyself the nations are scattered. And your spoils shall be gathered together as the locusts are gathered, as when the ditches are full of them. The Lord is magnified, for he hath dwelt on high: he hath filled Sion with judgment and justice.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Ecce apparébit Dóminus super nubem cándidam, Et cum eo Sanctórum míllia: habens in vestiménto, et in fémore suo scriptum * Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium.
<r>℣.</r> He shall appear and not lie; though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will surely come. Rex regum, et.
976505fe4d:
<h>Lectio ii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adjuváre dignétur.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 33:6, 14-15</r>
<c>E</c>rit fides in tempóribus tuis: divítiæ salútis sapiéntia et sciéntia: timor Dómini ipse est thesáurus ejus. Contérriti sunt in Sion peccatóres, possédit tremor hypócritas: quis póterit habitáre de vobis cum igne devoránte? quis habitábit ex vobis cum ardóribus sempitérnis? Qui ámbulat in justítiis, et lóquitur veritátem,
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium ii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Béthlehem cívitas Dei summi, ex te éxiet Dominátor Israël, et egréssus ejus sicut a princípio diérum æternitátis, et magnificábitur in médio univérsæ terræ: Et pax erit in terra nostra * Dum vénerit.
<r>℣.</r> Loquétur pacem in géntibus, et potéstas ejus a mari usque ad mare. Dum vénerit..
f0e10d3900:
<h>Lesson 2</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the only-begotten Son of God vouchsafe to bless and help us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 33:6, 14-15</r>
And there shall be faith in thy times: riches of salvation, wisdom and knowledge: the fear of the Lord is his treasure. The sinners in Sion are afraid, trembling hath seized upon the hypocrites. Which of you can dwell with devouring fire? which of you shall dwell with everlasting burnings? He that walketh in justices, and speaketh truth, that casteth away avarice by oppression, and shaketh his hands from all bribes, that stoppeth his ears lest he hear blood, and shutteth his eyes that he may see no evil.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Béthlehem cívitas Dei summi, ex te éxiet Dominátor Israël, et egréssus ejus sicut a princípio diérum æternitátis, et magnificábitur in médio univérsæ terræ: Et pax erit in terra nostra * Dum vénerit.
<r>℣.</r> He shall speak peace unto the Gentiles, and shall have dominion from sea to sea. Dum vénerit..

<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<c>Q</c>ui prójicit avarítiam ex calúmnia, et éxcutit manus suas ab omni múnere, qui obtúrat aures suas ne áudiat sánguinem, et claudit óculos suos ne vídeat malum. Iste in excélsis habitábit, muniménta saxórum sublímitas ejus: panis ei datus est, aquæ ejus fidéles sunt. Regem in decóre suo vidébunt óculi ejus, cernent terram de longe.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>C</c>ónditor alme síderum,
Ætérna lux credéntium,
Christe, Redémptor ómnium,
Exáudi preces súpplicum.

<h>Q</h>ui cóndolens intéritu
Mortis períre sǽculum,
Salvásti mundum lánguidum,
Donans reis remédium,

<h>V</h>ergénte mundi véspere,
Uti sponsus de thálamo,
Egréssus honestíssima
Vírginis matris cláusula.

<h>C</h>uius forti poténtiæ
Genu curvántur ómnia;
Cæléstia, terréstria
Nutu faténtur súbdita.

<h>T</h>e deprecámur, hágie,
Ventúre judex sǽculi,
Consérva nos in témpore
Hostis a telo pérfidi.

<h>L</h>aus, honor, virtus, glória,
Deo Patri, et Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.

<r>Jer 23</r>
<c>B</c>ehold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign, and shall be wise, and shall execute judgement and justice in the earth.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor the law-giver from his loins, until he that shall be sent cometh. * And unto him shall the longing of the Gentiles be.
<r>℣.</r> His eyes shall be bright with wine, and his teeth white with milk.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>B</c>right builder of the heavenly poles,
Eternal light of faithful souls,
Jesus, Redeemer of mankind,
Our humble prayers vouchsafe to mind.

<h>W</h>ho, lest the fraud of hell’s black king
Should all men to destruction bring,
Didst, by an act of generous love,
The fainting world’s physician prove.

<h>W</h>ho, that thou mightst our ransom pay
And wash the stains of sin away,
Wouldst from a Virgin’s womb proceed
And on the cross a victim bleed.

<h>W</h>hose glorious power, whose saving name
No sooner any voice can frame,
But heaven and earth and hell agree
To honour them with trembling knee.

<h>T</h>hee, Christ, who at the latter day
Shalt be our Judge, we humbly pray
Such arms of heavenly grace to send
As may thy Church from foes defend.

<h>B</h>e glory given and honour done
To God the Father and the Son
And to the Holy Ghost on high,
From age to age eternally.
Amen.

<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.

<r>Isa 51:1-3</r>
<c>A</c>udíte me qui sequímini quod justum est, et quǽritis Dóminum: atténdite ad petram unde excísi estis, et ad cavérnam laci, de qua præcísi estis. Atténdite ad Abraham estis. patrem vestrum, et ad Saram, quæ péperit vos: quia unum vocávi eum, et benedíxi ei, et multiplicávi eum. Consolábitur ergo Dóminus Sion, et consolábitur omnes ruínas ejus: et ponet desértum ejus quasi delícias, et solitúdinem ejus quasi hortum Dómini. Gáudium et lætítia inveniétur in ea, gratiárum áctio et vox laudis.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium i</h>
<r>℟.</r> Cánite tuba in Sion, vocáte gentes, annuntiáte pópulis, et dícite: * Ecce Deus Salvátor noster advéniet. Annuntiáte in fínibus terræ : et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt, di cite. — Ecce Deus.

<r>Isa 51:1-3</r>
Give ear to me, you that follow that which is just, and you that seek the Lord: look unto the rock whence you are hewn, and to the hole of the pit from which you are dug out. Look unto Abraham your father, and to Sara that bore you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and multiplied him. The Lord therefore will comfort Sion, and will comfort all the ruins thereof: and he will make her desert as a place of pleasure, and her wilderness as the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of praise.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Rom 4:1-5</r>
<c>Q</c>uid ergo dicémus invenísse Abraham patrem nostrum secúndum carnem? Si enim Abraham ex opéribus justificátus est, habet glóriam, sed non apud Deum. Quid enim dicit Scriptúra? Crédidit Abraham Deo: et reputátum est illi ad justítiam. Ei autem, qui operátur, merces non imputátur secúndum grátiam, sed secúndum débitum. Ei vero, qui non operátur, credénti autem in eum, qui justíficat ímpium, reputátur fides ejus ad justítiam secúndum propósitum grátiæ Dei.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium iv</h>
<r>℟.</r> Ecce jam venit plenitúdo témporis, in quo misit Deus Fílium suum in terras, natum de Vírgine, factum sub lege * Ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redímeret.
<r>℣.</r> Propter nímiam caritátem suam, qua diléxit nos Deus, Fílium suum misit in similitúdinem carnis peccáti. Ut eos, qui.
7e4c6659e0:

<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.

<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Rom 4:1-5</r>
What shall we say then that Abraham hath found, who is our father according to the flesh. For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory, but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice. Now to him that worketh, the reward is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt. But to him that worketh not, yet believeth in him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is reputed to justice, according to the purpose of the grace of God.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Behold, the fullness of the time is come, wherein God hath sent forth His Son into the world, born of a Virgin, made under the law; * To redeem them that were under the law.
<r>℣.</r> God, for His great love wherewith He loved us, hath sent His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh. To redeem them.

Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum. Beatitúdo ergo hæc in circumcisióne tantum manet, an étiam in præpútio? Dícimus enim quia reputáta est Abrahæ fides ad justítiam. Quómodo ergo reputáta est? in circumcisióne, an in præpútio? Non in circumcisióne, sed in præpútio.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 54:1-3</r>
<c>L</c>auda stérilis quæ non paris: decánta laudem, et hinni quæ non pariébas: quóniam multi fílii desértæ magis quam ejus, quæ habet virum, dicit Dóminus. Diláta locum tentórii tui, et pelles tabernaculórum tuórum exténde, ne parcas: longos fac funículos tuos, et clavos tuos consólida. Ad déxteram enim, et ad lævam penetrábis, et semen tuum gentes hereditábit, et civitátes desértas inhabitábit.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium i</h>
<r>℟.</r> Cánite tuba in Sion, vocáte gentes, annuntiáte pópulis, et dícite: * Ecce Deus Salvátor noster advéniet. Annuntiáte in fínibus terræ : et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt, di cite. — Ecce Deus.
dce06b7094:
<h>Lesson 1</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the everlasting Father bless us with an everlasting blessing.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 54:1-3</r>
Give praise, O thou barren, that bearest not: sing forth praise, and make a joyful noise, thou that didst not travail with child: for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband, saith the Lord. Enlarge the place of thy tent, and stretch out the skins of thy tabernacles, spare not: lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes. For thou shalt pass on to the right hand, and to the left: and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles, and shall inhabit the desolate cities.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, call together the nations, tell it out among the people, and say: * Ecce Deus Salvátor noster advéniet. Annuntiáte in fínibus terræ : et in ínsulis, quæ procul sunt, di cite. — Ecce Deus.
bf3d27f0bd:
<h>Lectio ii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adjuváre dignétur.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 54:4-6</r>
<c>N</c>oli timére, quia non confundéris, neque erubésces: non enim te pudébit, quia confusiónis adolescéntiæ tuæ obliviscéris, et oppróbrii viduitátis tuæ non recordáberis ámplius. Quia dominábitur tui qui fecit te, Dóminus exercítuum nomen ejus: et redémptor tuus sanctus Israël, Deus omnis terræ vocábitur. Quia ut mulíerem derelíctam et mœréntem spíritu vocávit te Dóminus, et uxórem ab adolescéntia abjéctam, dixit Deus tuus.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium ii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Non auferétur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de fémore ejus, donec véniat qui mitténdus est * Et ipse erit exspectátio géntium.
<r>℣.</r> Pulchrióres sunt óculi ejus vino, et dentes ejus lacte candidióres. Et ipse erit.
44fdd8f5b6:

<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the only-begotten Son of God vouchsafe to bless and help us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 54:4-6</r>
Fear not, for thou shalt not be confounded, nor blush: for thou shalt not be put to shame, because thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt remember no more the reproach of thy widowhood. For he that made thee shall rule over thee, the Lord of hosts is his name: and thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of all the earth. For the Lord hath called thee as woman forsaken and mourning in spirit, and as a wife cast off from her youth, said thy God.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor the law-giver from his loins, until he that shall be sent cometh. * And unto him shall the longing of the Gentiles be.
<r>℣.</r> His eyes shall be bright with wine, and his teeth white with milk. And unto him.
2f1feba69f:
<h>Lectio iii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Spíritus Sancti grátia illumináre dignétur sensus et corda nostra.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 54:7-9</r>
<c>A</c>d punctum in módico derelíqui te, et in miseratiónibus magnis congregábo te. In moménto indignatiónis abscóndi fáciem meam parúmper a te, et in misericórdia sempitérna misértus sum tui: dixit redémptor tuus Dóminus. Sicut in diébus Noë istud mihi est, cui jurávi ne indúcerem aquas Noë ultra super terram: sic jurávi ut non iráscar tibi, et non íncrepem te.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium iii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Me opórtet mínui, illum autem créscere: qui autem post me venit, ante me factus est * Cujus non sum dignus corrígiam calceamentórum sólvere.
<r>℣.</r> Ego baptizávi vos aqua: ille autem baptizábit vos Spíritu Sancto. Cujus non sum.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Cujus non sum.
3a37f18f5f:
<h>Lesson 3</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the grace of the Holy Spirit vouchsafe to enlighten our senses and hearts.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Isa 54:7-9</r>
For a, small moment have I forsaken thee, but with great mercies will I gather thee. In a moment of indignation have I hid my face a little while from thee, but with everlasting kindness have I had mercy on thee, said the Lord thy Redeemer. This thing is to me as in the days of Noe, to whom I swore, that I would no more bring in the waters of Noe upon the earth: so have I sworn not to be angry with thee, and not to rebuke thee.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> I must decrease, but He must increase; He it is Who, coming after me is preferred before me; * Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.
<r>℣.</r> I baptize you with water; but He shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost. Whose shoe's latchet.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. Whose shoe's latchet.

<n>S. Agnétis Virg. et Mart.</n>
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>O</c>mnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui infírma mundi éligis, ut fórtia quæque confúndas: concéde propítius; ut, qui beátæ Agnétis Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ solémnia cólimus, ejus apud te patrocínia sentiámus.

a5516d0c08:
<h>Prayer of the Saint</h>
<n>S. Agnétis Virg. et Mart.</n>
<c>L</c>et us pray.
O Almighty and everlasting God, Who hast chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty, mercifully grant unto us that we who keep the solemn feast of thy blessed Virgin and Martyr Agnes, may feel the power of her intercession with thee.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

This householder, then, for the cultivation of his vineyard, goeth out early in the morning, and at the third hour, and the sixth hour, and the ninth hour, and the eleventh hour, to hire labourers into his vineyard. Thus the Lord, from the beginning to the end of the world, ceaseth not to gather together preachers for the instruction of His faithful people. The early morning of the world was from Adam until Noah; the third hour from Noah until Abraham; the sixth hour from Abraham until Moses; the ninth hour from Moses until the coming of the Lord; the eleventh hour from the coming of the Lord until the end of the world. At this eleventh hour are sent forth as preachers the Holy Apostles, who have received full wages, albeit they be come in late.

<n>S. Scholásticæ Virg.</n>
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui ánimam beátæ Vírginis tuæ Scholásticæ ad ostendéndam innocéntiæ viam in colúmbæ spécie cælum penetráre fecísti: da nobis ejus méritis et précibus ita innocénter vívere; ut ad ætérna mereámur gáudia perveníre.

c1471f05c3:
<h>Commemoration</h>
<n>S. Scholásticæ Virg.</n>
<c>L</c>et us pray.
O God, Who, to show the way of the undefiled, wast pleased that the soul of thy blessed Virgin Scholastica should fly to heaven in a bodily shape, like a dove, mercifully grant unto us thy servants, for her sake, and at her petition, worthily to attain unto thine everlasting joy.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
ca19e39662:
<h>Lectio i</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Evangélica léctio sit nobis salus et protéctio.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Cum introísset Jesus Caphárnaum, accéssit ad eum centúrio, rogans eum, et dicens: Dómine, puer meus jacet in domo paralýticus, et male torquétur. Et réliqua.
<r>Homilía sancti Augustíni Epíscopi. (Lib. 2. de Consénsu Evangelistárum, cap. 20.)</r>
<c>V</c>ideámus, utrum sibi de hoc servo centuriónis Matthǽus Lucásque conséntiant. Matthǽus enim dicit: Accéssit ad eum centúrio, rogans eum, et dicens: Puer meus jacet in domo paralýticus. Cui vidétur repugnáre quod ait Lucas: Et cum audísset de Jesu, misit ad eum senióres Judæórum, rogans eum ut veníret, et sanáret servum ejus. At illi cum veníssent ad Jesum, rogábant eum sollícite, dicéntes ei: Quia dignus est ut hoc illi præstes: díligit enim gentem nostram, et synagógam ipse ædificávit nobis.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
5e87044d54:
<h>Lesson 1</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the Gospel reading be our salvation and protection.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
At that time, when Jesus had entered into Capharnaum, there came to him a centurion, beseeching him and saying: Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, and is grievously tormented. And so on.
<r>Homilía sancti Augustíni Epíscopi. (Lib. 2. de Consénsu Evangelistárum, cap. 20.)</r>
Videámus, utrum sibi de hoc servo centuriónis Matthǽus Lucásque conséntiant. Matthǽus enim dicit: Accéssit ad eum centúrio, rogans eum, et dicens: Puer meus jacet in domo paralýticus. Cui vidétur repugnáre quod ait Lucas: Et cum audísset de Jesu, misit ad eum senióres Judæórum, rogans eum ut veníret, et sanáret servum ejus. At illi cum veníssent ad Jesum, rogábant eum sollícite, dicéntes ei: Quia dignus est ut hoc illi præstes: díligit enim gentem nostram, et synagógam ipse ædificávit nobis.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
6999f2f4ea:
<h>Lectio ii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Divínum auxílium máneat semper nobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>J</c>esus autem ibat cum illis: et cum jam non longe esset a domo, misit ad eum centúrio amícos, dicens: Dómine, noli vexári: non enim Feria Vi. sum ut sub tectum meum intres. Si enim hoc ita gestum est, quómodo erit verum, quod Matthǽus narrat: Accéssit ad eum quidam centúrio, cum ipse non accésserit, sed amícos míserit: nisi diligénter adverténtes intellegámus Matthǽum non omnímodo deseruísse usitátum morem loquéndi? Lectio iii, ergo absúrde Matthǽus, étiam quod vulgo possit intéllegi, per álios facto accéssu centuriónis ad Dóminum, compéndio dícere vóluit: Accéssit ad eum centúrio. Verúmtamen non negligénter intuénda est étiam sancti Evangelístæ altitúdo mýsticæ locutiónis, secúndum quam scriptum est in Psalmo: Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini. <h>Hymnus</h>
<c>C</c>hriste, qui lux es et dies,
Noctis tenébras détegis,
Lucísque lumen créderis,
Lumen beátum prǽdicans.

<h>P</h>recámur sancte Dómine,
defénde nos in hac nocte:
Sit nobis in te réquies,
Quiétam noctem tríbue.

<h>N</h>e gravis somnus írruat,
Nec hostis nos subrípiat,
Nec caro illi conséntiens
Nos tibi reos státuat.

<h>O</h>culi somnum cápiant,
Cor ad te semper vígilet:
Déxtera tua prótegat
Fámulos, qui te díligunt.

<h>D</h>efénsor noster áspice,
Insidiántes réprime,
Gubérna tuos fámulos,
<n>Ad hunc Vers. genuflectatur</n>
Quos Sánguine mercátus es.

<h>M</h>eménto nostri, Dómine,
In gravi isto córpore:
Qui es defénsor ánimæ,
Adésto nobis, Dómine.

<h>P</h>ræsta Pater omnípotens,
Per Jesum Christum Dóminum,
Qui tecum in perpétuum
Regnat cum Sancto Spíritu.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Custódi nos, Dómine, ut pupíllam óculi.
<r>℟.</r> Sub umbra alárum tuárum prótege nos.

<h>Hymn</h>
<c>C</c>hriste, qui lux es et dies,
Thou dost lay bare the darkness of night,
And art believed the light of light,
Proclaiming the blessed light.

We pray thee, holy Lord,
defénde nos in hac nocte:
Sit nobis in te réquies,
Grant us a quiet night.

<h>N</h>e gravis somnus írruat,
Nec hostis nos subrípiat,
Nec caro illi conséntiens
Nos tibi reos státuat.

<h>O</h>culi somnum cápiant,
Cor ad te semper vígilet:
May thy right hand protect
The servants that love thee.

Look upon us, our Defender,
Hold back them that lie in wait,
Govern thy servants,
<n>Ad hunc Vers. genuflectatur</n>
Whom thou hast purchased with thy Blood.

Remember us, O Lord,
In gravi isto córpore:
Thou who art the defender of the soul,
Be present with us, O Lord.

<h>P</h>ræsta Pater omnípotens,
Per Jesum Christum Dóminum,
Qui tecum in perpétuum
Regnat cum Sancto Spíritu.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Keep us, O Lord, as the apple of thine eye.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>S</c>ummi largítor prǽmii,
Spes qui es única mundi,
Preces inténde servórum,
Ad te devóte clamántium.

<h>N</h>ostra te consciéntia
Grave offendísse monstra:
Quam emúndes, supplicámus,
Ab ómnibus piáculis.

<h>S</h>i rénuis, quis tríbuet?
Indúlge, quia potens es:

Fac nos precámur, Dómine.

e6c3bd05ee:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>he fast, as taught by holy lore,
We keep in solemn course once more:
The fast to all men known, and bound
In forty days of yearly round.

<h>T</h>he law and seers that were of old
In diverse ways this Lent foretold,
Which Christ, all seasons’ King and Guide,
In after ages sanctified.

<h>M</h>ore sparing therefore let us make
The words we speak, the food we take,
Our sleep and mirth, —and closer barred
Be every sense in holy guard.

<h>A</h>void the evil thoughts that roll
Like waters o’er the heedless soul;
Nor let the foe occasion find
Our souls in slavery to bind.

<h>I</h>n prayer together let us fall,
And cry for mercy, one and all,
And weep before the Judge’s feet,
And his avenging wrath entreat.

<h>T</h>hy grace have we offended sore,
By sins, O God, which we deplore;
But pour upon us from on high,
O pardoning One, thy clemency.

<h>R</h>emember thou, though frail we be,
That yet thine handiwork are we;
Nor let the honour of thy name
Be by another put to shame.

<h>F</h>orgive the sin that we have wrought;
Increase the good that we have sought:
That we at length, our wanderings o'er,
May please thee here and evermore.

<h>G</h>rant O thou Blessed Trinity,
Grant, O Essential Unity,
That this our fast of forty days
May work our profit and thy praise.
Amen.

<h>D</h>ans tempus acceptábile,

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>J</c>esu, salvation’s Sun Divine,
Within our inmost bosoms shine,
With light all darkness drive away
And give the world a better day.

<h>N</h>ow days of grace with mercy flow,
O Lord, the gift of tears bestow,
To wash our stains in every part,
Whilst heavenly fire consumes the heart.

<h>R</h>ise, crystal tears, from that same source
From whence our sins derive their course;
Nor cease, till hardened hearts relent,
And softened by your streams, repent.

<h>B</h>ehold, the happy days return,
The days of joy for them that mourn;
May we of their indulgence share,
And bless the God that grants our prayer.

<h>M</h>ay heaven and earth aloud proclaim
The Trinity’s almighty fame;
And we, restored to grace, rejoice
In newness both of heart and voice.
Amen.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> kind Creator, bow thine ear
To mark the cry, to know the tear
Before thy throne of mercy spent
In this thy holy fast of Lent.

<h>O</h>ur hearts are open, Lord, to thee:
Thou knowest our infirmity;
Pour out on all who seek thy face
Abundance of thy pardoning grace.

<h>O</h>ur sins are many, this we know;
Spare us, good Lord, thy mercy show;
And for the honour of thy name
Our fainting souls to life reclaim.

<h>G</h>ive us the self-control that springs
From discipline of outward things,
That fasting inward secretly
The soul may purely dwell with thee.

<h>W</h>e pray thee, Holy Trinity,
One God, unchanging Unity,
That we from this our abstinence
May reap the fruits of penitence.
Amen.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Joël 2</r>
<c>C</c>onvertímini ad me in toto corde vestro, in jejúnio, et fletu, et planctu: et scíndite corda vestra, et non vestiménta vestra, ait Dóminus omnípotens.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>I</c>am Christe sol justítiæ,
Mentis diéscant ténebræ:
Virtútum ut lux rédeat,
Terris diem cum réparas.

<h>D</h>ans tempus acceptábile,
Et pǽnitens cor tríbue,
Convértat ut benígnitas
Quos longa suffert píetas.

<h>Q</h>uiddámque pæniténtiæ
Da ferre, quamvis grávium,
Majóre tuo múnere,
Quo démptio fit críminum.

<h>D</h>ies venit, dies tua,
In qua reflórent ómnia:
Lætémur in hac ad tuam
Per hanc redúcti grátiam.

<h>T</h>e rerum univérsitas,
Clemens, adóret, Trínitas,
Et nos novi per véniam,
Novum canámus cánticum.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Scuto circúmdabit te véritas ejus.
<r>℟.</r> Non timébis a timóre noctúrno.
5aeccc9f69:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Joël 2</r>
<c>B</c>e converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning. And rend your hearts, and not your garments, said the almighty Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>J</c>esu, salvation’s Sun Divine,
Within our inmost bosoms shine,
With light all darkness drive away
And give the world a better day.

<h>N</h>ow days of grace with mercy flow,
O Lord, the gift of tears bestow,
To wash our stains in every part,
Whilst heavenly fire consumes the heart.

<h>R</h>ise, crystal tears, from that same source
From whence our sins derive their course;
Nor cease, till hardened hearts relent,
And softened by your streams, repent.

<h>B</h>ehold, the happy days return,
The days of joy for them that mourn;
May we of their indulgence share,
And bless the God that grants our prayer.

<h>M</h>ay heaven and earth aloud proclaim
The Trinity’s almighty fame;
And we, restored to grace, rejoice
In newness both of heart and voice.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> His truth shall compass thee with a shield.
<r>℟.</r> Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>A</c>udi, benígne Cónditor,
Nostras preces cum flétibus,
In hoc sacro jejúnio
Fusas quadragenário.

<h>S</h>crutátor alme córdium,
Infírma tu scis vírium:
Ad te revérsis éxhibe
Remissiónis grátiam.

<h>M</h>ultum quidem peccávimus,
Sed parce confiténtibus:
Ad laudem tui nóminis
Confer medélam lánguidis.

<h>S</h>ic corpus extra cónteri
Dona per abstinéntiam,
Ieiúnet ut mens sóbria
A labe prorsus críminum.

<h>P</h>ræsta, beáta Trínitas,
Concéde, simplex Únitas;
Ut fructuósa sint tuis
Ieiuniórum múnera.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Ángelis suis Deus mandávit de te.
<r>℟.</r> Ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
ac20c4305a:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Joël 2</r>
<c>B</c>e converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning. And rend your hearts, and not your garments, said the almighty Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>O</c> kind Creator, bow thine ear
To mark the cry, to know the tear
Before thy throne of mercy spent
In this thy holy fast of Lent.

<h>O</h>ur hearts are open, Lord, to thee:
Thou knowest our infirmity;
Pour out on all who seek thy face
Abundance of thy pardoning grace.

<h>O</h>ur sins are many, this we know;
Spare us, good Lord, thy mercy show;
And for the honour of thy name
Our fainting souls to life reclaim.

<h>G</h>ive us the self-control that springs
From discipline of outward things,
That fasting inward secretly
The soul may purely dwell with thee.

<h>W</h>e pray thee, Holy Trinity,
One God, unchanging Unity,
That we from this our abstinence
May reap the fruits of penitence.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> For he hath given his angels charge over thee.
<r>℟.</r> To keep thee in all thy ways.

The deep meaning is given; but what is considered is the lie because men do not understand the way in which that signification, which is a truth, is set forth but the falsehood is plainly expressed, and believed. <c>L</c>ocútus est Dóminus Judǽis, dicens: Ego vado. Christo enim Dómino mors proféctio fuit illo, unde vénerat, Ego, inquit, vado, et quærétis me, non desidério, sed ódio. <r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Locútus est Jesus ad turbas, et ad discípulos suos, dicens: Super cáthedram Móysi sedérunt scribæ et pharisǽi. Omnia ergo quæcúmque díxerint vobis, serváte, et fácite: secúndum ópera vero eórum nolíte fácere. Et réliqua. Infra Hebdom. Ii. sancti Hierónymi Presbýteri (Lib, in cap. Matth,) mansuétius, quid benígnius Dómino? Tentátur a pharisǽis, confringúntur insídiæ eórum, et secúndum Psalmístam: Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum: et nihilóminus propter sacerdótii nóminis dignitátem hortátur pópulos, ut subiciántur eis, non ópera, sed doctrínam considerántes. Quod autem ait, Super cáthedram Móysi sedérunt scribæ et pharisǽi: per cáthedram, doctrínam Legis osténdit.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Lectio ii</h>

<c>E</c>rgo et illud quod dícitur in Psalmo: In cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit: et, Cáthedras vendéntium colúmbas evértit: doctrínam debémus accípere. Alligant enim ónera grávia et importabília, et impónunt in húmeros hóminum, dígito autem suo nolunt ea movére. Hoc generáliter advérsus omnes magístros, dictum est, qui grávia jubent, et minóra non sciunt. Lectio iii, enim phylactéria sua, et magníficant fímbrias. Dóminus cum dedísset mandáta Legis per Móysen, ad extrémum íntulit: Ligábis ea in manu tua, et erunt immóta ante óculos tuos. Et est sensus: Præcépta mea sint in manu tua, ut ópere compleántur: sint ante óculos tuos, ut die ac nocte meditéris in eis. Hoc pharisǽi male interpretántes, scribébant in membránis decálogum Móysi, id est, decem verba Legis, complicántes ea et ligántes in fronte, et quasi corónam cápiti faciéntes: ut semper ante óculos moveréntur.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

She, then, yielding to the intensity of her motherly love, besought the Saviour, saying, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one at thy right hand and the other at thy left hand, in thy kingdom. Although it was a mistake, it was a mistake of love. For a mother's love knoweth no moderation. Yet, although it was a greedy prayer, that was a pardonable greed, which hungered, not for riches, but for grace. Neither was that request shameless which sought, not her own good, but her children's. Remember that she was a mother. Think how that she was a mother.

<c>Q</c>uare illum córripis? Quia tu doles, quod peccáverit in te? Absit. Si amóre tui id facis, nihil facis: si amóre illíus facis, óptime facis. Dénique in ipsis verbis atténde, cujus amóre id fácere débeas, utrum tui, an illíus. Si te audíerit, inquit, lucrátus es fratrem tuum. Ergo propter illum fac, ut lucréris illum. Sic faciéndo lucráris: nisi fecísses, períerat. Quid est ergo, quod pleríque hómines ista peccáta contémnunt, et dicunt: Quid magnum feci? In hóminem peccávi. Noli contémnere: quod in hóminem peccásti.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.

<c>Q</c>uid audívimus, fratres? Ecce templum illud figúra adhuc erat, et ejécit inde Dóminus omnes qui sua quærébant, qui ad núndinas vénerant. Et quæ ibi vendébant illi? 2b7230db6c:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>P</c>ange, lingua, gloriósi
Prœlium certáminis,
Et super Crucis trophǽo
Dic triúmphum nóbilem,
Quáliter Redémptor orbis
Immolátus vícerit.

<h>D</h>e paréntis protoplásti
Fraude Factor cóndolens,
Quando pomi noxiális
Morsu in mortem córruit,
Ipse lignum tunc notávit,
Damna ligni ut sólveret.

<h>H</h>oc opus nostræ salútis
Ordo depopóscerat,
Multifórmis proditóris
Ars ut artem fálleret,
Et medélam ferret inde,
Hostis unde lǽserat.

<h>Q</h>uando venit ergo sacri
Plenitúdo témporis,
Missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
Atque ventre virgináli
Carne amíctus pródiit.

<h>V</h>agit infans inter arcta
Cónditus præsépia:
Membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat:
Et manus, pedésque, et crura
Stricta cingit fáscia.

<h>G</h>lória, et honor Deo
Usqueqáque Altíssimo,
Una Patri, Filióque;
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas,
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.
58ff6dd241:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, my tongue, the glorious battle
Sing the last, the dread affray;
O'er the cross, the victor's trophy,
Sound the high triumphal lay:
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a victim won the day.

<h>G</h>od, his Maker, sorely grieving
That the first-made Adam fell,
When he ate the fruit of sorrow,
Whose reward was death and hell,
Noted then this wood, the ruin
Of the ancient wood to quell.

<h>F</h>or the work of our salvation
Needs would have his order so,
And the multiform deceiver's
Art by art would overthrow,
And from thence would bring the med'cine
Whence the insult of the foe.

<h>W</h>herefore, when the sacred fullness
Of the appointed time was come,
This world's Maker left his Father,
Sent the heav'nly mansion from,
And proceeded, God Incarnate,
Of the Virgin's holy womb.

<h>W</h>eeps the infant in the manger
That in Bethlehem's stable stands;
And his limbs the Virgin Mother
Doth compose in swaddling bands,
Meetly thus in linen folding
Of her God the feet and hands.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

Inclyto Paráclito:

Where his life-blood shall be spilled.

Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:

All created things repeat.

<h>Lectio ii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adjuváre dignétur.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Jer 12:4-7</r>
<c>U</c>squequo lugébit terra, et herba omnis regiónis siccábitur, propter malítiam habitántium in ea? consúmptum est ánimal, et vólucre, quóniam dixérunt: Non vidébit novíssima nostra. Si cum pedítibus currens laborásti, quómodo conténdere póteris cum equis? cum áliter in terra pacis secúrus fúeris, quid fácies in supérbia Jordánis? Nam et fratres tui, et domus patris tui, ipsi pugnavérunt advérsum te, et clamavérunt post te plena voce: ne credas eis, cum locúti fúerint tibi bona. Dominica in
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium ii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Fratres mei elongavérunt se a me: et noti mei * Quasi aliéni recessérunt a me.
<r>℣.</r> Dereliquérunt me próximi mei, et qui me novérunt. Quasi aliéni recessérunt.
5ad2983904:
<h>Lesson 2</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the only-begotten Son of God vouchsafe to bless and help us.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Jer 12:4-7</r>
How long shall the land mourn, and the herb of every field wither for the wickedness of them that dwell therein? The beasts and the birds are consumed: because they have said: He shall not see our last end. If thou hast wearied with running with footmen, how canst thou contend with horses? and if thou hast been secure in a land of peace, what wilt thou do in the swelling of the Jordan? For even thy brethren, and the house of thy father, even they have fought against thee, and have cried after thee with full voice: believe them not when they speak good things to thee. I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance: I have given my dear soul into the land of her enemies.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> My brethren stand afar off from me, and they which have known me * Make themselves strange unto me, and leave me.
<r>℣.</r> My neighbours forsake me, and mine acquaintance Make themselves strange.

<h>Lectio iii</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Spíritus Sancti grátia illumináre dignétur sensus et corda nostra.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Jer 12:7-10</r>
<c>R</c>elíqui domum meam, dimísi hereditátem meam: dedi diléctam ánimam meam in manu inimicórum ejus. Facta est mihi heréditas mea quasi leo in silva: dedit contra me vocem, ídeo odívi eam. Numquid avis díscolor heréditas mea mihi? numquid avis tincta per totum? veníte, congregámini omnes béstiæ terræ, properáte ad devorándum. Pastóres multi demolíti sunt víneam meam, conculcavérunt partem meam: dedérunt portiónem meam desiderábilem in desértum solitúdinis.
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<h>Responsorium iii</h>
<r>℟.</r> Atténde, Dómine, ad me, et audi voces adversariórum meórum: * Numquid rédditur pro bono malum, quia fodérunt fóveam ánimæ meæ? Recordáre quod stéterim in conspéctu tuo, ut lóquerer pro eis bonum, et avérterem indignatiónem tuam ab eis.
5bc3d5ab01:
<h>Lesson 3</h>
<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.
<r>Blessing.</r> May the grace of the Holy Spirit vouchsafe to enlighten our senses and hearts.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<r>Jer 12:7-10</r>
I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance: I have given my dear soul into the land of her enemies. My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: is hath cried out against me, therefore have I hated it. Is my inheritance to me as a speckled bird? Is it as a bird died throughout? come ye, assemble yourselves, all the beasts of the earth, make haste to devour. Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my portion under foot: they have changed my delightful portion into a desolate wilderness.
Thus saith the Lord God: Be converted to me, and you shall be saved.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Responsory</h>
<r>℟.</r> Give heed to me, O Lord, and hearken to the voice of them that contend with me. * 20 Shall evil be rendered for good, because they have digged a pit for my soul? Remember that I have stood in thy sight, to speak good for them, and turn away thy indignation from them.

<h>Lectio iv</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
<r>Benedictio.</r> Deus Pater omnípotens sit nobis propítius et clemens.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>c</c>ausam discámus, et quam ob rem passus fúerit unigénitus Dei Fílius considerémus; non jam erubescámus, sed mirábitur bonitátem, humanitatemque ejus, et gloriábitur nos quoque, quemádmodum Paulus, in cruce. Non enim Dóminus ipse propter seípsum, sed nos in illo patiebátur! Nam hóminum peccátum ingens erat, et hoc malum totum occupáverat orbem. <r>℣.</r> Factus sum in derísum omni pópulo meo, cánticum eórum tota die. Vide, Dómine, iniquitátes.

<c>A</c>uróra lucis rútilat,
Cælum láudibus íntonat,
Mundus exsúltans iúbilat,

<h>C</h>um Rex ille fortíssimus,
Mortis confráctis víribus,
Pede concúlcans tártara,
Solvit a pœna míseros.

<h>I</h>lle qui clausus lápide
Custodítur sub mílite,
Triúmphans pompa nóbili,
Victor surgit de fúnere.

Et inférni dolóribus,
Quia surréxit Dóminus,

2f37d98191:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>O</c> thou, the heavens' eternal King,
Creator, unto thee we sing,
With God the Father ever One,
Co-equal, co-eternal Son.

<h>T</h>hy hand, when first the world began,
Made in thine own pure image man,
And linked to Adam, sprung from earth,
A living soul of heavenly birth.

<h>A</h>nd when by craft the envious foe
Had marred thy noblest work below,
Clothed in our flesh, thou didst restore
The image thou hadst made before.

<h>S</h>o that thou might redeem man
Whom thou hadst made
And us to God might thou wouldst unite
Through thy union with the flesh.

<h>O</h>nce wast thou born of Mary's womb;
And now, new-born from out the tomb,
O Christ, thou bidd'st us rise with thee
From death to immortality.

<h>E</h>ternal Shepherd, thou dost lave
Thy flock in pure baptismal wave,
That mystic bath, that grave of sin,
Where ransomed souls new life begin.

<h>R</h>edeemer, thou for us didst deign
To hang upon the Cross of pain,
And give for us the lavish price
Of thine own blood in sacrifice.

<h>G</h>rant, Lord, in thee each faithful mind
Unceasing paschal joy may find;
And from the death of sin set free
Souls newly born to life by thee.

<h>T</h>o Thee Who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, Thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>T</c>he morn had spread her crimson rays,
When rang the skies with shouts of praise;
Earth joined the joyful hymn to swell,
That brought despair to vanquished hell.

<h>H</h>e comes victorious from the grave,
The Lord omnipotent to save,
And brings with him to light of day
The saints who long imprisoned lay.

<h>V</h>ain is the cavern’s three-fold ward —
The stone, the seal, the armed guard;
O death, no more thine arm we fear,
The Victor’s tomb is now thy bier.

<h>L</h>et hymns of joy to grief succeed,
We know that Christ is risen indeed;
We hear his white-robed angel’s voice,
And in our risen Lord rejoice.

<h>W</h>ith Christ we died, with Christ we rose,
When at the font his name we chose;
Oh, let not sin our robes defile,
And turn to grief the paschal smile.

<h>T</h>o God the Father let us sing,
To God the Son, our risen King,
And equally let us adore
The Spirit, God forevermore.

3069a80bf4:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Rom 6</r>
<c>C</c>hristus resúrgens ex mórtuis jam non móritur, mors illi ultra non dominábitur. Quod enim mórtuus est peccáto, mórtuus est semel: quod autem vivit, vivit Deo.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>A</c>d cenam Agni próvidi,
Et stolis albis cándidi,
Post tránsitum maris Rubri,
Christo canámus Príncipi.

<h>C</h>uius corpus sanctíssimum,
In ara crucis tórridum,
Cruóre ejus róseo
Gustándo vívimus Deo.

<h>P</h>rotécti Paschæ véspere
A devastánte Angelo,
Erépti de duríssimo
Pharaónis império.

<h>I</h>am Pascha nostrum Christus est,
Qui immolátus agnus est:
Sinceritátis ázyma,
Caro ejus obláta est.

<h>O</h> vere digna hóstia,
Per quam fracta sunt tártara,
Redémpta plebs captiváta,
Réddita vitæ prǽmia.

<h>C</h>onsúrgit Christus túmulo,
Victor redit de bárathro,
Tyránnum trudens vínculo,
Et Paradísum réserans.

<h>Q</h>uǽsumus, Auctor ómnium,
In hoc pascháli gáudio,
Ab omni mortis ímpetu
Tuum defénde pópulum.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
Cum Patre et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Mane nobíscum, Dómine, allelúja.
<r>℟.</r> Quóniam advesperáscit, allelúja.
acae1fa516:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Rom 6</r>
<c>K</c>nowing that Christ rising again from the dead, dieth now no more, death shall no more have dominion over him. For in that he died to sin, he died once; but in that he liveth, he liveth unto God.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>A</c>t the Lamb’s high feast we sing
Praise to our victorious King,
Who hath washed us in the tide
Flowing from his piercèd side.

<h>P</h>raise we him whose love divine
Gives the guests his blood for wine,
Gives his body for the feast,
Love the victim, love the priest.

<h>W</h>here the paschal blood is poured,
Death’s dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel’s hosts triumphant go
Through the wave that drowns the foe.

<h>C</h>hrist, the Lamb whose blood was shed,
Paschal victim, paschal bread;
With sincerity and love
Eat we manna from above.

<h>M</h>ighty victim from the sky,
Powers of hell beneath thee lie;
Death is conquered in the fight;
Thou hast brought us life and light.

<h>N</h>ow thy banner thou dost wave;
Vanquished Satan and the grave;
Angels join his praise to tell —
See o’erthrown the prince of hell.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Stay with us, O Lord, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> Because it is towards evening, alleluia.

f9941239a1:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>H</c>ail, thou who man's Redeemer art,
Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

<h>W</h>hat nameless mercy thee o'ercame,
To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

<h>T</h>he realms of woe are forced by thee,
Its captives from their chains set free;
And thou, amid thy ransomed train,
At God's right hand dost victor reign.

<h>L</h>et mercy sweet with thee prevail,
To cure the wounds we now bewail;
Oh, bless us with thy holy sight,
And fill us with eternal light.

<h>P</h>aschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

<h>H</h>ymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Keep us, O Lord, as the apple of thine eye.
<r>℟.</r> Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.

<c>M</c>ódicum est hoc totum spátium, quo præsens pérvolat sǽculum. Unde dicit idem ipse Evangelísta in Epístola Octavam Pascha. sua: Novíssima hora est. Ideo namque áddidit: Quia vado ad Patrem: quod ad priórem senténtiam referéndum est, ubi ait: Módicum et jam non vidébitis me: non ad posteriórem, ait: El íterum módicum, et vidébitis me. Eúndo quippe ad Patrem, factúrus erat ut eum non vidérent. Lectio ii, telis ergo ait: Módicum, et jam non vidébitis me; qui eum corporáliter tunc vidébant: quia itúrus erat ad Patrem, et eum deínceps mortálem visúri non erant, qualem, cum ista loquerétur, vidébant. Quod vero áddidit: Et íterum módicum, et vidébitis me: univérsæ promísit Ecclésiæ, sicut univérsæ promísit: Ecce ego vobíscum sum usque ad consummatiónem sǽculi. Non tardat Dóminus promíssum.
Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<c>A</c>d insinuándam quoque veritátem Domínicæ resurrectiónis, notándum nobis est quid Lucas réferat, dicens: Convéscens, præcépit eis ab Jerosólymis ne discéderent. Et post pauca: Vidéntibus illis, elevátus est, et nubes suscépit eum ab óculis eórum. Notáte verba, signáte mystéria. Convéscens elevátus est. Comédit, et ascéndit: ut vidélicet per efféctum comestiónis, véritas patésceret carnis. Marcus vero, priúsquam cælum Dóminus ascéndat, eum de cordis atque infidelitátis durítia increpásse discípulos mémorat. Qua in re quid considerándum est, nisi quod idcírco Dóminus tunc discípulos increpávit, cum eos corporáliter relíquit, ut verba, quæ recédens díceret, in audiéntium árctius impréssa remanérent?

<r>℣.</r> Pray, sir, a blessing.

Now confirm to our minds the trustworthiness of the fact that our Lord did indeed rise again from the dead, it is well for us to remark one of the statements of Luke (Acts i. 4.) “Eating together with them, He commanded them that they should not (1 John xiv. 16, 17 xvi. 7.) depart from Jerusalem and a little afterward: “While they beheld, He was taken up, and a cloud received Him out of their sight.” Consider these words, note well these mysteries. After “eating together with them He was taken up.” He ate and ascended: that the fact of His eating might show the reality of the Body in Which He went up. But Mark telleth us that before the Lord ascended into heaven, He upbraided His disciples; with their unbelief and hardness of heart. From this I know not why we should gather, but that the Lord then upbraided His disciples, for whom He was about to be parted in the body, to the end that the words which He spoke unto them as He left them might be the deeper imprinted on their hearts.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

On the solemn Feast of the Passover the cause of our joy was that Christ was risen again. This day we rejoice because that He is ascended up into heaven. We call to mind and justly celebrate that day whereon our lowly nature was, in the Person of Christ, borne up high above all the heavenly armies, above all the circles of Angels, beyond the heights of all the Powers, even to where Christ is sitting on the right hand of the Father. Our foundations are laid, and our house is built upon this succession of the works of God and His grace is made more wonderful by this, that, though the visible Object of worship is removed from among men, the faith of the Church doth not grow weak, nor her hope wavering, nor her love cold.
But thou, O Lord, have mercy on us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
